title: Are you ready to quit your job?
intro: Not a verdict, and not permission. A read on which of five places you are actually standing, based on what has happened rather than how it feels.
og_line: Eight questions and an honest read on where you actually stand.

cta.title: The number underneath this
cta.label: Work out the real cost
cta.blurb: Most of this question is arithmetic wearing a feeling. What it would cost to start, and what you would have to sell to cover it.

questions.q: Has anyone outside your own circle paid you for this?

options.a: A couple, and it felt like luck
Not yet. There is nothing to buy
No, and I have not asked anyone

questions.q: Months of your own costs sitting in the bank:

options.a: I could not tell you without checking

questions.q: When you picture handing in your notice, the first feeling is:

options.a: A flat calm. I have pictured it a lot

questions.q: What is actually stopping you today?

options.a: Nothing concrete, and that bothers me
I do not know what to build first
I want one more quarter of proof

questions.q: The last twelve weeks, on this:

options.a: Shipped something and talked to buyers

questions.q: If it earned half your salary for a year, you would:

options.a: Realise I have never done that sum

questions.q: Who knows you are thinking about this?

options.a: Everyone. I have said it out loud
People asked, and I changed the subject

questions.q: A year from now, the outcome you would find hardest:

options.a: Still standing in exactly this spot
Having gone and run out of money
Having gone too early and killed a good idea

results.name: Still dreaming about it
results.headline: You want it, and nothing has been tested yet.
results.body: Wanting it is not the same as being close to it, and there is no shame in that. Nothing here has met a real customer, which means nothing here has been disproved either.
results.cost: Time. The idea keeps its shine for exactly as long as nobody tries to buy it.

results.name: Quietly testing it
results.headline: It exists in small, and a few people have said yes.
results.body: You have proof that somebody wants it, at a scale that cannot pay you yet. This is the most useful place to be and the least comfortable.
results.cost: Patience. The evidence is real but thin, and thin evidence is easy to over-read.

links.label: What you would have to sell

results.name: Stalled on purpose
results.headline: You could move and you have decided not to yet.
results.body: There is a reason you are waiting and it is probably a good one. Worth being honest about whether the reason is the mortgage or the fear, because they need different answers.
results.cost: Momentum. A pause you keep extending stops being a decision and becomes a habit.

results.name: Closer than you are admitting
results.headline: The numbers work and you are still saying next year.
results.body: Revenue exists, the gap is smaller than you say out loud, and the thing standing in the way is the size of the jump rather than the maths.
results.cost: The story you tell people about why not yet. It gets more convincing every time you tell it.

results.name: Better off keeping the job
results.headline: For now, and that is a real answer.
results.body: The runway is short, the demand is unproven, and going now would mean pricing in a panic. Plenty of businesses got built at nights and weekends first.
results.cost: Nothing, yet. This is the cheapest place to be wrong.
